phrases.text: Drying clothes indoors makes the whole house damp.
And a tumble dryer costs money every time you run it. So you put up a washing line.
Dig a hole in the lawn, and drop in a ground socket.
Fill it with quick-setting concrete, and hold it level while it sets.
The rotary line slots in, opens like an umbrella, and the washing goes out.
Then it rains on your washing. So you build a roof over it.
But under the roof there's no breeze. Nothing dries. So you add a fan.
The fan needs power, and the cable across the lawn trips everyone up. So you put a wind turbine on the roof.
But down here, the fence and the house block the wind. The turbine barely turns.
So you lift the whole thing up on a tower.
Now you can't reach your washing. So you run a pulley line from the back door to the top.
Up there it's so windy, the socks blow away. So you add a net.
And the turbine makes far more power than one fan needs. So you plug something in.
Congratulations. You built a tower so you wouldn't need a tumble dryer. There is now a tumble dryer at the top.
